revela_isp_core.description: The board's display pipeline: the Bayer ISP -- pedestal off, illuminant balanced, Hamilton-Adams demosaic, colour matrix -- then a display curve and the mark. Geometry and CFA phase ride the bayerlink header, so they arrive as stream context, never registers.

inputs.name: isp_in
inputs.description: Raw Bayer from the bayerlink receiver. bit_depth above is the depth samples ARRIVE at here; the depth they arrived on the WIRE is the header's, run-time and any of 8/10/12/14/16, and the receiver has already scaled them to this one. Change the sensor, not this number.

outputs.name: isp_out
outputs.description: Tone-mapped RGB, three channels in one word: R low, G mid, B high. The word's width is TRACED, not declared -- each block's output is whatever its model produces, and that is the next block's input.

isp.description: Raw Bayer in, linear RGB out: what any Bayer sensor on this board needs. Its input port states the stream it takes, built here for 12-bit frames up to 1920x1080.

rgb_gamma.description: The 2.2 display curve, this design's output encoding for HDMI, and its reset: a freshly loaded bitstream shows a gamma-correct picture before anything is written. The knots are in the units gamma OUTPUTS, which the knot declaration owns: 0..2**out_bits, so 0..256 for the 8-bit display output. A curve in the wrong units does not fail loudly -- the values truncate into the register and the tone curve becomes a sawtooth.

logo.description: The mark, from block RAM, keyed over the corner of the picture.
